summary.lead: Official summary (Congressional Research Service, Reported to House):

blocks.text: This bill authorizes the National Park Service (NPS) to enter into a one-time agreement with the Gateway Arch Park Foundation to host private events at the Gateway Arch National Park and its buildings for a period of up to five years. The NPS manages the park, located in St. Louis, Missouri, and its buildings, such as the Arch Visitor Center and the Old Courthouse.

The bill outlines the terms and conditions that must be included in the agreement. The bill also requires private events hosted at the park or its buildings to be consistent with the park's purposes and compatible with NPS programs. Such events may not (1) degrade the integrity, appearance, or purposes of the park; or (2) take place during times or in locations that prevent or disrupt public use or access to the park or its buildings.

The NPS must charge a fee to cover the cost of wear and tear resulting from the private events. The NPS may recover all costs incurred as a result of the private events, including maintenance, utilities, administrative expenses, security, and personnel costs.
The bill terminates the NPS's authority to enter and carry out an agreement with the foundation seven years after the enactment of this bill.

The Gateway Partnership Act would let the National Park Service sign a one-time agreement with the Gateway Arch Park Foundation to host private events at the Gateway Arch National Park in St. Louis, Missouri, and its buildings, such as the Arch Visitor Center and the Old Courthouse. The agreement could last up to five years.

The bill sets out the terms the agreement must include. Any private event held at the park or its buildings has to fit the park's purposes and work alongside the park service's programs. Events cannot damage the park's integrity, appearance, or purposes, and they cannot be scheduled at times or in places that stop or disrupt the public from using or getting to the park or its buildings.

The park service must charge a fee to cover the wear and tear caused by private events. It can also recover all costs connected to those events, including maintenance, utilities, administrative expenses, security, and staff time.
The park service's authority to make and carry out this agreement with the foundation ends seven years after the bill becomes law.
